writeup.headline: Dow rates Sell on thin margins, negative free cash flow and a stretched balance sheet despite a Q3 beat.
writeup.thesis: Dow scores 36, a Sell, held down mainly by weak quality and balance sheet factors. Gross margin is just 6.4%, FCF margin is -0.6%, the diluted share count is up 2.0% year on year, and cash covers only 0.24 of debt while FCF is negative. Growth is mixed: latest-quarter revenue growth of 13.0% year on year sits against a TTM revenue decline of 7.7%. Valuation scores 28: P/S of 0.6 is low in absolute terms, but the FCF yield is 5.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and P/S sits near the middle of the last 61 month-ends (cheaper than at 34, more expensive than at 27). Trend (53) and news (61) are firmer, helped by a Q3 beat, polyethylene price increases and the price 14.4% above its 50-day average, but they do not offset the fundamentals.
key_risks: Negative free cash flow alongside net debt, with cash covering only 0.24 of debt
Very thin gross margin of 6.4% leaves little cushion if chemical pricing weakens
Q3 volume slipped 1% with weakness in Asia Pacific, and Q4 EBITDA guided flat at about $1.5B
Pending securities class action and derivative suits, plus unresolved Sadara joint venture talks with Aramco
Shares 20.9 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and 18.5% below the 52-week high
what_would_change: A 9-point score gain would lift the rating to Hold, most likely via a return to positive free cash flow that improves quality, balance sheet and valuation scores
Delivery of the $700 million Transform to Outperform benefits and the planned polyethylene price increases, turning the TTM revenue decline into growth
A 7-point drop would mean Strong Sell, for example if the recent price strength fades and the trend score falls or guidance turns negative
Further debt build or more share dilution would weigh further on the balance sheet and quality scores
